items.stem: In STRIDE, which category covers an attacker pretending to be another legitimate user?

options.rationale: Correct: spoofing is impersonating another identity.
Repudiation is denying having performed an action.
Denial of service is making a resource unavailable.
Information disclosure is exposing data to unauthorised parties.

items.explanation: Correct: impersonating another identity is the Spoofing category in STRIDE.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO elements must a data-flow diagram show for threat modelling to find boundary threats? (Select TWO)

options.text: Trust boundaries where the level of trust changes
options.rationale: Correct: trust boundaries are where many threats arise and must be marked.

options.text: External entry points into the system
options.rationale: Correct: entry points define the attack surface to analyse.

options.text: The office seating plan of the team
options.rationale: Seating has no bearing on data-flow threats.
The roadmap is irrelevant to the DFD's security analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: trust boundaries and entry points are the DFD elements that drive boundary threat discovery.

items.stem: After enumerating many threats with limited budget, what is the right next step?

options.text: Rank them by likelihood and impact and mitigate the highest risks first
options.rationale: Correct: risk ranking directs limited resources to the biggest risks first.

options.text: Mitigate them in the order they were written down
options.rationale: Discovery order does not reflect risk.

options.text: Treat all threats as equally urgent
Ignore the low-likelihood high-impact ones by default
options.rationale: High-impact threats may warrant mitigation despite low likelihood.

items.explanation: Correct: prioritising by likelihood and impact focuses limited resources on the highest risks.
